First listed 2026-05-22 · episode or wrap

Walmart & Target Signal Consumer Stress as the 10-Year Yield Hits 4.6% | The Weekly Wrap

Eisman clarifies a meaningful risk reduction: he still sees strong corporate earnings but trims positions after long yields cross 4.5%. He identifies consumer and housing pressure, contrasts semiconductor strength with software disruption, and distinguishes current private-equity valuation damage from later refinancing losses. NVIDIA and Walmart releases support key contemporary premises. The extrapolation that private software equity must be worth at least 50% less remains unverified, and the 2027 refinancing forecast is still open.

Source · 5:00-6:15 ↗
SpeakerSteve Eisman
Stanceconditional

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Qualification: Utility cash flow, regulation, debt and demand can also change; the NextEra-Dominion transaction details are not independently verified here.

Conditional reasoning

Present value equals the sum of cash flows discounted by the required return; increasing that return lowers value. This does not prove the empirical cause of any specific utility return.

  • Fixed expected cash distributions
  • Higher required discount rate, all else equal

How he reasons here

  • Separate recession assessment from valuation and discount-rate risk.
  • Distinguish earnings beats from absolute growth and forward guidance.
  • Separate private-equity valuation losses from private-credit defaults.
  • Consider policy rescue risk when exiting short positions.
